main_text.head: UBBONIS EMMI STATVS REIPVBLICÆ duarum civitatum Atticæ & Laconicæ succincta delineatio.
main_text.p: CIvitatum Gracarum florentibus ejus gentis rebus longe clarissima fuerunt Athenæ & Lacedæmon, velut oculi duo inter cateras emicantes, æmula inter sese, & de principatu non gloriæ solum, sed etiam potentiæ decertantes: accidit que ut plurimum, ut ad harum motus & contentiones universa fere Græcia in diversa studia scinde-retur. Ita fit, ut qui harum status ignarus sit, infeliciter in cognoscendis Græcorum rebus bello & pace gestis versetur. Utriusque vero statum & rempubl. peculiaribus libellis delineatam summus autor, quo nemo propius rem nosse poterat; Xenophon reliquit, & multis sæculis post eum Plu-
main_text.notes: The large initial is C, so the first word is "Civitatum". The running head and any signature are not printed on this page. Bottom left shows faint marks and a red stain on the left edge, which I took to be show-through or stamps and did not transcribe. Two words are hyphenated at line end: "floren-tibus" and "scinde-retur", both with printed hyphens. The text ends with the catchword "Plu-" on the last line; the word continues on the next page. Spelling is as printed, including "cateras", "Gracarum" and "reliquit".
